title: Alzheimer’s disease GWAS — interactive colocalization Manhattan plot
text:
NoteHow to use





Hover your mouse in any variant of a significant locus: all variants of that locus will turn red and the box will show the summary of colocalization of that locus. Double-click to clear the highlight. For busiest regions you can use the zoom tool to help separate the labels.
The background points are variants outside the colocalization windows and are not interactive. To keep the scale legible, the plot shows only variants with p < 1e-4 and the y axis was truncated on the top because of APOE locus.

Full table












NoteComo a convergência é calculada





Convergence = at least one gene in common between the genes that colocalized on this analysis (genes_significant) and the union of literature sources (BigBrain eQTL/sQTL, Bellenguez, SingleBrain). Divergence = there’s literature for the locus, but none of the genes coincides. No comparison = none of the sources covers this locus (includes all 19 new loci from consensus meta-analysis).

title: A multi-context colocalization atlas of Alzheimer’s Disease loci
text:
How to use it

Manhattan (interactive) — Manhattan plot of the whole genome, hover through a locus to show colocalization details.
Colocalization Explorer — Full colocalization bubble plot, you can filter by dataset family and locus.
Development vs Adult — Dev/adult contrast, with highlight to dev-only pairs.
Cell Type Specificity — cell type specificity heatmap (sceQTL).
Locus Table — browsable table, with an overview of results by locus.

title: A multi-context colocalization atlas of Alzheimer’s Disease loci
text:
A peek at the methodology
The results shown correspond to Bayesian colocalization (coloc.abf, PP.H4 ≥ 0,8) between the consensus AD GWAS (2026) and 23 xQTL datasets — BigBrain (adult, eQTL/sQTL), DevBrain (fetal, eQTL/sQTL), SingleBrain (7 major cell types) e GTEx (15 tissues). Colocalization windows were defined as 500 kb centered at the reported lead variant of each locus. Full methods will be published soon in a paper. Pipeline: nf_coloc.
